user_journeys.title: Create an encrypted document, restart, find it, and reopen it

acceptance_criteria.statement: The Android app completes the journey through its installed UI after a process-style restart.
The iOS simulator app completes the journey through its installed UI after relaunch.

Only authorized verified active metadata is searchable and opens the intended document.

defects.summary: The Android shell initially lacked Room runtime and bundled SQLite ABI dependencies; repair attempt 1 added the required compile/runtime dependencies and the complete construction run passed.
Visual inspection of the first installed J1 pass found header/status-bar overlap; platform insets were applied and the complete installed journey passed again.
Run 33834830361 could not tap Search behind the keyboard. Keyboard-aware layout, an accessible Done action and visible-result assertions passed installed J1 on candidate and main.
Added one narrowly verified Pixel Launcher ANR dismissal with regression tests; application ANRs remain failures. Both accepted J1 runs required zero infrastructure recoveries.
Removed recursive Xcode build-phase testing; existing guarded workflow runs named installed XCTest explicitly, retains failure evidence and packages the exact tested app.
Serialized all mutable shared vault runtime calls and close on one queue; source-level regression assertion and installed journey passed. This is not a general concurrency stress-test claim.

After J1 passed and PR #2 merged, a separate writer re-added aleil-ios-test.yml at c78b82beae06c194a77a4256610150689ea97447. It uses an unrestricted runner input and lacks the public-repository allocation guard, violating the locked single-workflow/free-execution rules. Product preflight 33838952381 failed. User direction/concurrent-writer coordination is required; the verified 1c6ab92 snapshot remains accepted.
